definition: Depicted scene participation, including sustained flashbacks, direct narration, and explicitly authored letters. Passing mentions, brief recaps, recipient-only references, future plans, and dream likenesses are excluded. The author card marks explicit framing appearances, not every narrated chapter.
primary_source: Georgian text in data/chapters/chapter-*.json. Attached English rows sometimes cross chapter boundaries.

chapters.notes: Explicit author/prologue voice and self-identification7–9. Tariel and the three heroes are invoked, not depicted in a story scene.
Coronation and banquet: actors shown32–69. Shermadin70 is only assigned as tomorrow’s prospective hunting helper and is not depicted acting here.
Hunt and wager72–83. Shermadin is not individually identified in the hunting action; the servants are collective. His possible continuous service from the assignment in2:70 is left unasserted.
Stranger’s encounter84–101, then Tinatin visits/counsels Rostevan102–119.
Tinatin’s private commission, Avtandil’s actual farewell exchange with Rostevan142–146, and Shermadin’s commission149–164.
Avtandil authors the charter and departs; Shermadin personally gathers the nobles and displays the letter175–176. Tinatin is merely remembered.

Avtandil meets the three brothers197–210; their narrated encounter depicts Tariel’s actions. He later follows Tariel and directly watches his reunion with Asmat221–227. No Shermadin here: English177 belongs to Georgian176 in chapter6.
Asmat and Avtandil’s confrontation, Tariel’s return, and the introduction/embrace. Rostevan in Tariel’s short hunting recap is not present.
The three speak together in the cave. Tinatin, Rostevan and hunters occur only within Avtandil’s short account and are excluded.

Sustained Indian-youth flashback shows Saridan, the royal parents, Nestan’s birth/growth, and Davar’s entrusted upbringing330. Asmat acts in both childhood331 and cave-frame revival322/326; Avtandil explicitly weeps in the frame326.

First sight of Nestan344, Parsadan/queen attend Tariel’s illness, Asmat mediates and visits; frame Avtandil is the other weeping knight345. Anonymous doctors are not identified as the later specific Tariel_surgeon profile.
Nestan is the explicit letter author376–379; Tariel reads; Asmat speaks directly380.
Tariel writes the answer; Asmat relays advice, rejects jewels, accepts a ring, and leaves382–386. Nestan is letter addressee and subject of Asmat’s brief reported earlier command, not depicted here.
Tariel authors and dispatches the letter387–388, then returns to banquet389–390. Ramaz is recipient only; Parsadan is praised inside the letter.
The pavilion meeting391–399 depicts all three. Opening reference to having come from the king’s palace391 does not depict Parsadan acting.
Ramaz authors the answer401; Tariel reads, summons troops and reviews them402–405. Parsadan’s royal standard404 and Nestan remembered as sun are mentions only.
Asmat summons and introduces Tariel406–410; Nestan and Tariel speak and swear fidelity411–419. No Parsadan scene.

Campaign, the specific informer’s warning, battle and Ramaz’s capture. Saridan is only mentioned in the informant’s brief explanation of past care; no sustained Saridan flashback. Gifts dispatched to Parsadan462 do not depict recipient-only king.

Return/reception, Ramaz’s pardon and court banquet. Queen speaks/is greeted and Nestan directly exchanges looks with Tariel. Asmat’s arrival is Georgian20:490, although displaced English19:489 appears one chapter early.
Georgian490–492 depicts Asmat’s arrival and exchange;493–496 is Nestan’s authored letter. English494–496 fainting/revival belongs to Georgian21:497–499 and does not add Avtandil to20.
Georgian497–501 depicts Tariel’s fainting and revival, Asmat’s care and Avtandil’s response;502 resumes the narrative with Asmat’s delivery of the bracelet. Nestan is mentioned, not shown.
Tariel authors his reply503–505; Asmat (the continuing unnamed maid) leaves506. Nestan is recipient and a fleeting dream likeness506, both excluded from actual depicted presence.

notes: 507–513: Tariel meets both Indian sovereigns. 514–515: the King of Khwarazm responds to the marriage embassy. Nestan and the prince are discussed/planned spouses, not depicted participants; the prince is only the object of the summons at516.

517–547: Asmat brings Tariel to Nestan and conducts him away; the lovers speak at length. Tariel is the active first-person narrator; Avtandil is not individually depicted acting or speaking in this chapter.
548–552: Parsadan welcomes the bridegroom’s arrival and gives orders;553–556: Tariel/Asmat/Nestan meet;557–558: Tariel kills the prince;561–566: Parsadan and Tariel exchange messages.

567–571 and582–590: Tariel and Asmat speak and depart.572–581 is an enacted, sustained flashback through Asmat’s testimony: Parsadan threatens Davar, Davar beats and abducts Nestan, then kills herself. These are depicted actions rather than names in a passing recap.

591–612: Tariel encounters and befriends Pridon.598 Georgian explicitly depicts Tariel’s surgeon removing the arrows and dressing Pridon’s injuries. Asmat is not individually depicted here; she is only known from the preceding chapter to accompany Tariel. Anonymous members of the camp do not automatically give Asmat a filled circle.
613–621: Tariel and Pridon fight together and return in triumph. The cousins are uncarded figures. No individually depicted Asmat scene occurs.

622–649: Tariel and Pridon confer, hunt, plan the search and part.625–628 is an extended direct-observation flashback of Nestan landing and escaping in a boat, so Nestan is counted.650–657: Tariel directly addresses Asmat/remaining attendants;659–671 returns to Avtandil/Tariel/Asmat speaking and acting in the cave frame.

672–727: Avtandil returns; Shermadin greets him and gives news to Rostevan and Tinatin; both sovereigns receive Avtandil. Tariel and Asmat occur in Avtandil’s summary of the search, not as chapter participants.

728–773: Avtandil visits the vizier, who petitions Rostevan and returns to Avtandil. The vizier is treated as Sograt under the main card catalog’s established identification; Ustasra is a title, not another person. Tariel/Asmat are objects of Avtandil’s explanation, not present participants.
774–787: Avtandil speaks with Shermadin and entrusts the household/testament to him. Rostevan, Tinatin and Tariel are discussed only.
788–807: Avtandil writes his own testament, which counts as his direct authored speech;808: he hands it to Shermadin and embraces him. Recipient Rostevan is not depicted in this chapter.
809–812: Avtandil prays and leaves;812 explicitly depicts Shermadin being sent back, weeping.

813–829 Georgian: Rostevan summons and speaks with the vizier/Sograt;827–829: Shermadin delivers the testament. Avtandil is absent; the news of his flight and the fact that his earlier testament is read are not a new depicted Avtandil scene. The text of the testament is not repeated here.

830–865: Avtandil travels to the cave and speaks with Asmat. Tariel’s departure and promises are briefly recounted by Asmat; Tariel is not present or directly observed. This agrees with the prior Tariel mask.
866–905: Avtandil finds, revives and speaks with Tariel. Asmat is discussed as a reason to return, but not yet encountered.

906–913 Georgian: Tariel directly narrates the lion/panther fight.914–915 Georgian explicitly depicts Avtandil weeping and answering; these rows have null/misaligned English, so primary Georgian is decisive. Nestan is only the metaphorically recalled beloved.
916–950: Tariel, Avtandil and Asmat reunite in the cave, eat and speak; the knights later travel together. Tinatin appears only in Avtandil’s short report of her permission.
951–968: Avtandil travels alone and sings to the heavenly bodies. Tinatin/Tariel are remembered or addressed in absence; Pridon is merely the destination, not a scene participant.

969–1024: Avtandil meets Pridon, tells his story, is hosted and departs.993–1008 is a compressed recap of Tariel and Arabia;1022–1023 briefly repeats the prior Nestan sighting rather than staging a new sustained flashback. Tariel, Nestan, Asmat, Rostevan and the hunters are excluded from this chapter’s presence mask.
1025–1060: Avtandil meets Usam, protects the caravan and receives the merchants’ thanks. Usam is distinct from Fatman’s husband Usen. Fatman/Nestan/Usen do not appear in the caravan scene.

1061–1080: Avtandil questions Usen’s gardener; the gardener directly reports to Fatman; she receives Avtandil.1070 explicitly says Usen is absent. Surkhavi is named as ruler, not depicted acting. Usam is not individually depicted merely because a merchant crowd remains present.

1081–1083 Georgian: Fatman alone is individually depicted, struggling with and voicing her desire. Avtandil is the object of her inward monologue, not described acting/speaking or directly observed in this chapter; therefore he receives no filled circle here.

chapters.notes: 1084–1089: Fatman writes and sends; Avtandil reads and responds in thought. Tinatin/Nestan are recalled, not depicted.
1095–1119: exchange of replies, Fatman/Avtandil meeting, Chashnagir confrontation and killing. Usen1120 is only mentioned.

1121–1212: Fatman sustained narration; Avtandil directly interrupts1137–1138,1211–1212. Full enacted retrospective scenes include Nestan, Usen, Sea King, and Chashnagir1205–1208. Sea King’s son1186 is described as away at war; no depicted scene.

1217–1243 contains informant’s enacted capture account, Roshak’s orders and actions, Dulardukht’s explicit quoted decision/custody. Rosan/Rodia1220–1221 are the children being raised (explicit care in the flashback). Fatman’s messenger1238–1239 is one of the two scouts and appears again1268–1269. Usen1215 is an absent reference, not action.
1270–1275: Fatman authors and hands over letter; 1276–1284 messenger enters Nestan’s prison and they converse. Avtandil is named inside letter and report, without direct scene presence.
1285–1291: Nestan authors letter. Fatman is addressed; Tariel and Dulardukht are mentioned, not depicted.

1292–1310: Nestan writes and cuts the veil;1311 messenger returns;1312–1317 Avtandil speaks with Fatman and sends Pridon’s attendants away. Tariel is only the letter’s recipient; Pridon only message recipient.
1318–1324: Avtandil authors letter;1325–1326 departure and Fatman/Usen farewell. Pridon is recipient only.
1327–1373: Avtandil reunites with Tariel, revives him, both meet Asmat and open treasury. Nestan is recalled via earlier letter, not newly authored or physically depicted.

1374–1389: journey with Asmat, meeting Pridon, hospitality, Asmat left at Pridon’s.1390–1392: three approach Kadjeti;1392 directly locates/visually presents the bright moon Nestan in the city. Included that brief observed presence, not just the search objective.
1393–1396: Pridon addresses his two companions in the ongoing council. Both addressed listeners count in this immediate scene, although only Pridon speaks.
1397–1401: Avtandil replies to Pridon and addresses both companions at the council. Hypothetical future actions are not additional people.
1402–1427: joint council, attack, Nestan rescue and greetings. Dulardukht is away and does not appear; no Rosan/Rodia battle invented.
1428–1447: Tariel’s message, Sea King and Fatman arrive, greetings/gifts/ship;1451–1453 Asmat embraces Nestan. Usen1431 is only a directed request recipient, without a depicted reception/action.
1463–1491: wedding and brotherly consultation. Asmat not individually depicted despite probable continued residence. Tinatin/Rostevan are discussed as absent people.
1496–1497: Asmat explicitly hosts in cave.1504–1548 Tariel’s message and Arabian reunion depict Rostevan/Tinatin and all three knights/Nestan. No named Shermadin or Sograt greeting.
1549–1578: Arabian wedding, gifts, farewells, sisters’ exchange, three knights’ departure. Asmat absent from individual action.

1579–1597 continues the three companions’ journey/meal begun1577–1578; Tariel and Nestan directly react to news. Parsadan/Davar/prince are only a brief recap; queen and Ramaz only a report about India, excluded under the brief-recap rule.
1598–1618: joint approach and Ramaz’s surrender.1620–1633: Nestan and Tariel enter India, queen embraces them; Avtandil/Pridon offer condolences1631. Parsadan is dead and mourned, not present.

1634–1664: enthronement, queen, Ramaz’s pardon, Asmat’s grant/marriage, brothers part;1662 Avtandil returns and sees/sits beside his sun Tinatin. Rostevan1658 is gift recipient only, not shown receiving it.
1665–1669: explicit poet’s authorial self-identification. Tariel1669 is a literary reference, not fictional scene participation.

editorial_note: Conservative scene-based masks. Source notes document borderline decisions; interaction correspondence and chapter appearance are different measures.
